decisions.reason: The prohibition on crazy effects and flashy transitions does not alter the existing requirement to use color to make captions and letters stand out.
The clean, simple visual-editing standard does not change the independently evaluated caption-font requirement.

Message 84 separately changes source selection by requiring all eight clips to come from one YouTube video, but that change is not a consequence of the clean visual-editing decision and is already represented.

Message 84 separately changes the substantive-moment standard, but the requirement that clips teach something or provide a lesson is independent of the visual-editing-style change and is already represented.
Message 84 separately refines narrative completeness, but capturing a complete moment is independent of the clean visual-editing-style change and is already represented.
The source decision addresses visual editing and does not modify the existing criterion for selecting moments with good hooks.
The candidate already requires an eight-clip trial batch, and the clean, simple visual-editing standard does not change its batch count or delivery obligation.
The visual-editing-style change does not alter the existing 20-to-120-second duration limits.
Message 84 repeats the target of 180 approved clips per month but does not change it, and the visual-editing-style decision has no necessary effect on that production target.
